title: Retire the auth documentation this site never grew into
description:
The presentability scan flagged FEATURE_PATTERNS.md as referenced by no other tracked file. Taken literally that is a one-file deletion, but the file was the visible end of a larger dead run: it was the only inbound reference to AUTH_PATTERNS.md, which was in turn the main reference to AUTH_UPGRADE.md — 668 lines describing a cookie-and-database auth abstraction in `app/lib/auth.ts`, a file that does not exist. Nor does `public/uploads/`. The Prisma schema has exactly one model, `Message`, written by the contact form, and there is no `getSession`, no sign-in, and no User or Session model anywhere in the app. The documentation described a project that was never built. Deleting only the flagged file would have silenced the scan while stranding the 623 lines it pointed at, unreachable and still wrong.

AUTH_PATTERNS.md and AUTH_UPGRADE.md are gone. FEATURE_PATTERNS.md stays, because not all of it was dead: the guidance on external services, seed imagery (Unsplash, and generating loremflickr URLs through the helper rather than by hand), file storage, and email is still accurate, and the contact pipeline it describes is real. Its authentication section is replaced by a short statement that this site has no auth and no auth abstraction to extend, so the next agent to look for one stops there instead of hunting for a file that was only ever documentation.

The file is also no longer an orphan, which is what drew the scan in the first place. AGENTS.md now carries a short index pointing at DATABASE.md and FEATURE_PATTERNS.md, added below the `next dev` marker block — that block is regenerated on every dev run, so hand-maintained content has to live outside it to survive.

One live link needed repair: DATABASE.md pointed at AUTH_UPGRADE.md when explaining what belongs in `.env.local`. The sentence now refers to third-party secrets generally, which is what it was really saying.
